\begin{example} \end{example}[Fubini--Study metric]

Source: petersen:page-0029 ↗ rem:pet-ch1-quotient-submersion ↗ ex:pet-ch1-sphere

1. ch1:1.3.4Scalar multiplication by $S^1\subset \mathbb {C}$ acts isometrically on $S^{2n+1}(1)\subset \mathbb {C}^{n+1}$. The quotient $S^{2n+1}/S^1=\mathbb {CP}^n$ carries the unique Fubini–Study metric making the quotient map a Riemannian submersion. For $n=1$ this is $S^3(1)\to \mathbb {CP}^1=S^2(1/2)$. \end{example}
